one_line: Sri Vaishnava acharya who systematized Vishishtadvaita and linked Sanskrit Vedanta with Tamil Alvar devotion.

appearance.age_look: Late 40s to early 50s, slim and ascetic but quietly robust, with a straight posture that hints at disciplined energy.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown South Indian complexion, calm almond-shaped eyes with a focused gaze, straight nose, neat trimmed brows, faint smile lines at the mouth and eyes, default expression a serene, compassionate seriousness as if mid-discourse.
appearance.hair: Clean-shaven head with a small, neatly indicated shikha (tuft) at the back crown; no facial hair; simple thin cotton headband in off-white encircling the head just above the ears, mostly hidden by the angle but visible at the temples.
appearance.costume: Traditional South Indian Sri Vaishnava acharya attire: a full-length off-white cotton dhoti (veshti) wrapped securely and brought up between the legs in panchakacham style, falling to the ankles, with a gold-ochre woven border; an upper cloth (uttariya) of light cream cotton with a muted maroon edge, draped over the left shoulder, across the chest and around the body so the end falls over the left arm; a narrower second angavastram of pale yellow, with a thin green stripe, folded neatly over the right shoulder; sacred thread (yajnopavita) suggested subtly beneath the drape without exposing the chest; clear but modest white and red vertical Sri Vaishnava tilaka marks on the forehead, with a small yellow line in the center; simple wooden tulasi bead necklace around the neck and a second slightly longer strand; bare arms from shoulder to wrist but otherwise fully covered torso and legs, with the cloth drawn high enough for ease of movement yet always modest; feet in simple brown leather sandals typical of the period.
appearance.signature: A long wooden palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark cord, held in his left arm against his body, and a smooth dark-brown wooden staff (danda) about shoulder-height with a plain rounded top, carried in his right hand.

ref_desc: Ramanuja is a serene, medium-brown, clean-shaven South Indian acharya in late middle age with a small shikha, Sri Vaishnava tilaka, off-white dhoti in panchakacham style, cream and pale-yellow upper cloths with maroon and gold-ochre borders, tulasi beads, brown sandals, and he carries a long wooden palm-leaf manuscript bundle and a dark wooden staff.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Ramanuja as a dignified South Indian Sri Vaishnava acharya: a slim, late middle-aged man with a medium-brown complexion, oval face, calm almond eyes and a serene, serious expression, clean-shaven head with a small shikha at the back, neat brows, and clear white-and-red Sri Vaishnava tilaka with a fine yellow center line on his forehead. He wears an off-white cotton dhoti in panchakacham style reaching his ankles, with a distinct gold-ochre border, and a cream upper cloth draped over the left shoulder and around the torso, edged in muted maroon, plus a second narrower pale-yellow angavastram with a thin green stripe folded over his right shoulder, so his torso and legs are always modestly covered. Suggest the sacred thread subtly under the drape without exposing the chest. Add simple wooden tulasi bead necklaces around his neck and plain brown leather sandals on his feet. In his left arm he cradles a long, bound bundle of dark-edged palm-leaf manuscripts, and in his right hand he holds a smooth dark wooden staff about shoulder height with a plain rounded top. Use a restrained palette of off-white, cream, maroon, gold-ochre, pale yellow and natural brown, and pose him front-facing, three-quarter, and back-facing to show the consistent arrangement of his dhoti, layered cloths, tilaka, beads, sandals, and the staff and manuscript bundle.
